chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Believer visits his family, so he sees what he loves, and it is veiled from him what he dislikes; and the Infidel visits his family, so he sees what he dislikes, and it is veiled from him what he loves.
He (peace be upon him) said: And among them is one who visits every Friday, and among them is one who visits according to the measure of his deeds.
ai.seo_question: How does the experience of the deceased visiting their family differ between a Believer and an Infidel in the afterlife?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the concept of *Ziyarat al-Mayyit* (visiting the deceased) in the Barzakh realm, illustrating how spiritual status dictates the deceased's perception of their family. The contrast between the Believer's joy and the Infidel's distress underscores the Shia understanding of the soul's continued connection to the worldly sphere, while the variable frequency of visits reflects the individual's accumulated merit (*amal*). This serves as a theological basis for the practice of families visiting graves to maintain spiritual bonds with the departed.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The (deceased) Believer visits his family, so he sees what he loves, and it is veiled from him what he dislikes from it; and the Infidel visits his family, so he sees what he dislikes, and it is veiled from him what he loves’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And from them is one who visits every Friday, and from them is one who visits upon the measurement of his (good) deeds’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hafs ibn af-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that a believing deceased person visits his family. He observes such matters that he loves and what he dislikes is kept hidden from him. A deceased unbeliever person also visits his family but observes what he dislikes and things that he loves are kept hidden from him. Certain ones of these people visit his family every Friday and others visit proportionate to their deeds.”
